A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FP4 training framework and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Renumbered tables and relocated appendix content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLaMA pretraining experiments, downstream accuracy, component ablations and tensor-distribution analyses, using FP4 emulation on FP8 hardware.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds downstream perplexity results in Table 3.

M1.justification: Equations (7)-(8) correct the stated DGE normalization: x-delta/2 becomes 2x/delta-1, and Equation (7)'s prefactor becomes delta/2. This revises the estimator specification while retaining the DGE/OCC framework and clipping threshold. The PDFs do not establish that implementations or training runs changed.

E1.justification: Table 3 adds evaluation on Pile10k and WikiText. DCLM training and the original downstream benchmarks remain; Lambada was already evaluated in v1 and gains explicitly named OpenAI and standard perplexity evaluations.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain BF16, MS-AMP FP8, Transformer Engine FP8 and direct-quantization variants. The added perplexity evaluation uses the existing BF16 comparator; no new competing method is evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds perplexity evaluation alongside the existing zero-shot accuracy evaluation for the 1.3B, 7B and 13B models. The stated 100B-token main training, 10B-token ablation training, batch sizes and optimization settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 6 retains the same precision, DGE, OCC and quantization-granularity ablations. The tensor-distribution and activation-outlier case studies are also unchanged, moving from Appendix C to Appendix D.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added perplexity results follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds average FP4/BF16 perplexities of 36.86/37.38, 35.62/35.06 and 33.99/33.69 for 1.3B, 7B and 13B models. Existing accuracy scores and plotted results remain unchanged. Appendix B adds theoretical speedup estimates, and Section 4.3 corrects the reported direction of the alpha trend.

T1.justification: Beyond correcting Equations (7)-(8), v2 adds a componentwise speedup/overhead derivation in Appendix B, a construction of the DGE function in C.1 and a smoothing/boundedness argument for clipping in C.3. The original vector-scaling proof is retained as C.2. These substantially expand the mathematical treatment.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: an FP4 LLM pretraining framework using DGE and OCC, comparable higher-precision performance, and validation up to 13B parameters and 100B tokens. Added evidence does not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 now correctly states that smaller alpha increases compensation and computational cost while improving accuracy, matching the retained Table 1 and Figure 6(c). Appendix B adds an efficiency-overhead tradeoff interpretation. Native-FP4 measurement and larger-scale validation limitations remain.

D1.justification: The introduction replaces a future code-release promise with a training-framework access link. Appendix B newly specifies FP8 sparse multiplication for OCC, where v1 described high-precision sparse multiplication. The CUDA quantization kernel and existing training details are retained; no underlying precision change is established.

R1.justification: v2 adds The Pile and WikiText references and substitutes a differently authored Q-ViT reference. The substantive positioning against prior quantized-training and inference methods remains unchanged. Most other bibliography changes update capitalization, publication venues and years.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section organization are retained. v2 makes localized wording corrections, adds appendix subsections and cross-references, updates bibliography formatting and adds the conference publication notice. The structural expansion primarily accompanies new technical content.

P2.justification: v2 adds the perplexity table and FLOP-breakdown table, renumbers the original FP4-format table from 3 to 4, and corrects the input/weight scaling labels in Figure 2. Existing plots are retained with local layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the estimator specification, resolves the contradictory alpha interpretation, adds perplexity evidence and supplies a framework access link. These gains are limited by flaws in the new theory: Appendix B's adjusted-speedup formula evaluates to about 3.03 rather than 2.95, and C.3 establishes boundedness without proving its claimed smoothing/clipping equivalence. The central empirical evidence and hardware limitations remain unchanged.
